reason: The cited evidence (E1, E3, E5) supports HfO2 scale formation, Zr diffusion, and reduced weight gain on a VZrHfNbTa HEA, but the material is not a Zr-alloy cladding, and the coating method is hot-press sintering, not PVD. The premise that PVD and heat treatment can control interdiffusion is entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Hf coating forms a dense, protective HfO2 scale during high-temperature oxidation
Zr diffuses into the Hf coating to form an Hf–Zr interlayer
The Hf–Zr interlayer ensures strong metallurgical bonding and adherence
The HfO2 scale significantly reduces oxidation weight gain vs. uncoated material
PVD and post-deposition heat treatment can control interdiffusion depth
